# Behavioral Design Specification: Alert Handler Ping Timer

## 1. Purpose

The module is a ping scheduler for an alert-handling subsystem. It generates ping requests to alert channels and escalation channels, monitors the corresponding responses, and reports failures when a ping is not answered in time or when an unsolicited response is observed.

The module has no software-programmable register interface. Its behavior is controlled by hardware inputs and by compile-time configuration.

## 2. Interface Overview

The module provides the following observable behavior:

- A clock and reset interface.
- A one-bit enable/start input.
- A per-alert enable vector, one bit per alert channel.
- A ping timeout value in cycles.
- A wait-cycle mask used to constrain randomized wait ranges.
- An entropy request/acknowledge/data interface used to refresh the randomization source.
- A ping request output vector for alert channels.
- A ping request output vector for escalation channels.
- A ping response input vector for alert channels.
- A ping response input vector for escalation channels.
- A separate ping failure output for alert channels.
- A separate ping failure output for escalation channels.

## 3. Reset and Enable Behavior

After reset, the module shall be quiescent with respect to ping generation: it shall not issue any alert ping requests or escalation ping requests.

The module shall remain in this quiescent state until the enable input is asserted. Once the enable input has been asserted:

- The module shall begin the ping schedule.
- The first ping operation shall be an alert ping attempt.
- The module shall not return to the quiescent state.
- Deasserting the enable input afterward shall not stop or pause the ping schedule.
- Only reset shall return the module to the quiescent state.

## 4. Ping Schedule

The module shall generate ping attempts that alternate between alert channels and escalation channels.

The sequence is:

1. Wait for a randomized interval.
2. Perform an alert ping attempt.
3. Wait for a randomized interval.
4. Perform an escalation ping attempt.
5. Repeat.

At any time, the module shall assert no more than one ping request among all alert and escalation request outputs. A ping request output shall be asserted only when a ping attempt is actively waiting for a response.

A ping attempt that is skipped because the selected alert channel is disabled shall not block the schedule. The module shall proceed to the next escalation ping attempt.

## 5. Randomization and Entropy

The module shall make ping timing and alert-channel selection unpredictable. It shall use an internal randomization source for:

- Choosing which alert channel to attempt next.
- Choosing how many cycles to wait before the next ping attempt.

The randomization source shall be refreshed periodically with externally supplied entropy.

When the refresh interval expires, the module shall assert the entropy request output and shall keep it asserted until the entropy acknowledge input is observed. When the acknowledge is observed, the module shall consume the entropy data and reload its refresh interval.

The entropy refresh operation shall be independent of whether the ping schedule has been enabled. The module may request entropy immediately after reset and at regular intervals afterward.

## 6. Randomized Wait Intervals

Before each ping attempt, the module shall enforce a randomized wait interval. The wait interval shall have a minimum value of at least 4 cycles.

The wait-cycle mask input may be used to limit the range of the wait interval. The module shall apply this mask to the randomized wait value. The mask shall be configured as a right-aligned mask with a numeric value of at least 7. If the mask does not satisfy this requirement, the module is not required to meet the stated wait-range behavior.

## 7. Alert Ping Operation

At each alert ping attempt, the module shall select one alert channel. The selected channel shall be held stable for the duration of that attempt.

If the selected alert channel is not enabled in the alert enable vector, the module shall:

- Not assert an alert ping request.
- Not start a ping timeout.
- Not report a ping failure for that channel.
- Proceed to the next escalation ping operation.

If the selected alert channel is enabled, the module shall:

- Assert the alert ping request for exactly that channel.
- Start the ping timeout countdown.
- Continue asserting the request until either a response from that channel is observed or the timeout expires.

The module shall not issue alert ping requests to disabled alert channels.

## 8. Escalation Ping Operation

At each escalation ping attempt, the module shall select an escalation channel in a fixed, deterministic order. The order shall cycle through all escalation channels repeatedly.

For the selected escalation channel, the module shall:

- Assert the escalation ping request for exactly that channel.
- Start the ping timeout countdown.
- Continue asserting the request until either a response from that channel is observed or the timeout expires.

Escalation pings shall always be generated once the ping schedule is enabled, regardless of the alert enable vector.

After an escalation ping attempt completes, the module shall advance to the next escalation channel in the cycle.

## 9. Response and Timeout Behavior

For both alert and escalation ping attempts, the following rules apply:

- If the response from the requested channel is observed before the timeout expires, the module shall consider the ping successful.
- The module shall deassert the request after the successful response is observed.
- No ping failure shall be reported for that ping attempt.
- If the timeout expires before a response is observed, the module shall report a ping failure on the corresponding failure output and deassert the request.
- If a response is observed in the same cycle in which the timeout expires, the module shall still report a ping failure.

A normal ping failure shall not stop the ping schedule. The module shall continue with subsequent ping attempts.

## 10. Spurious Response Detection

The module shall treat a ping response as spurious if it is asserted on a channel for which no ping request is currently active.

The following conditions shall cause a spurious-response failure:

- An alert response is received while no alert ping request is asserted.
- An alert response is received from an alert channel other than the one currently being requested.
- An escalation response is received while no escalation ping request is asserted.
- An escalation response is received from an escalation channel other than the one currently being requested.

A spurious alert response shall assert the alert ping failure output. A spurious escalation response shall assert the escalation ping failure output.

Spurious-response detection shall be active regardless of whether the ping schedule has been enabled. A spurious response shall not change the ping schedule by itself; the module shall continue its current behavior, with the failure output asserted for the cycle in which the spurious response is present.

## 11. Internal Integrity Lockdown

The module shall include internal consistency checking to protect against tampering or unexpected internal conditions.

If an internal inconsistency is detected, the module shall enter a terminal lockdown mode. In this mode:

- The module shall stop generating all new ping requests.
- The alert ping failure output shall remain continuously asserted.
- The escalation ping failure output shall remain continuously asserted.
- The enable input and response inputs shall not cause the module to leave this mode.

The module shall remain in lockdown until reset.

## 12. Configuration Constraints

The module is instantiated with a fixed number of alert channels and a fixed number of escalation channels.

The alert enable vector shall have one bit per alert channel.

The ping timeout value shall be expressed in cycles. A timeout value of zero shall be treated as an immediate timeout.

The wait-cycle mask shall be a right-aligned mask with a minimum value of 7; otherwise the wait interval behavior is outside the guaranteed operating range.

The module shall not require software intervention after reset other than the initial enable/start configuration.

# Behavioral Specification: Alert Handler Ping Timer

## Overview

This module implements the ping-generation and ping-monitoring behavior for the alert handler. It periodically sends line-test requests to alert receivers and escalation senders, randomizes the timing of those requests, and reports failures when a requested target does not respond in time or when an unsolicited response is observed.

The module has no register interface. It receives all configuration and status information as inputs and produces ping requests and failure indications as outputs.

## Reset and Initialization

- On reset, the module shall return to an inactive state.
- In the inactive state, the module shall not issue alert ping requests or escalation ping requests.
- The module shall remain inactive until the enable input is asserted.
- After the enable input has been asserted once, ping scheduling shall begin and shall continue until reset. Later deassertion of the enable input shall not stop the scheduling.

## Entropy and Randomization

- The module shall periodically request fresh entropy from the entropy distribution network.
- Whenever the entropy request is asserted and not yet acknowledged, the request shall remain asserted.
- When the entropy request is acknowledged, the module shall accept the entropy data provided at the same time and use it to re-randomize its internal ping-generation state.
- Entropy requests may occur before ping scheduling has been enabled and may also occur during any ping or wait phase.
- The entropy reseeding interval shall be fixed, with the same cycle-mask input used to shorten ping wait intervals also able to shorten the reseeding interval when configured.
- The module shall use a pseudo-random process to generate:
  - the amount of time to wait before the next ping, and
  - which alert channel is selected for the next alert ping.

## Ping Scheduling

- Once enabled, the module shall alternate between alert pings and escalation pings:
  1. wait a randomized interval,
  2. issue an alert ping,
  3. wait a randomized interval,
  4. issue an escalation ping,
  5. repeat.
- During a wait interval, no alert or escalation ping request shall be asserted.
- The randomized wait interval shall have a minimum spacing of at least four cycles.
- The wait-cycle mask input may be used to shorten the randomized wait interval for reduced counter ranges. When the mask is not intended to shorten the interval, it shall be set to all ones.
- At most one ping request shall be active at any time. The module shall not simultaneously request an alert ping and an escalation ping, and it shall not request pings for multiple channels of the same type at the same time.
- The same programmable ping timeout value shall be used for both alert pings and escalation pings.
- A ping request shall be held asserted until either the addressed target responds or the ping timeout expires.

## Alert Ping Behavior

- Before each alert ping phase, the module shall draw a pseudo-random alert index and a pseudo-random wait interval.
- The module shall check whether the selected alert index is enabled in the per-alert enable mask.
- If the selected alert index is not enabled:
  - the module shall not assert any alert ping request,
  - it shall not report a failure for that condition, and
  - it shall proceed to the escalation wait phase.
- If the selected alert index is enabled:
  - the module shall assert the alert ping request only for that selected alert channel,
  - it shall keep that request asserted until the selected alert responds or the ping timeout expires,
  - if the selected alert responds before timeout, the module shall proceed without reporting an alert ping failure, and
  - if the timeout expires before the selected alert responds, the module shall assert the alert ping failure indication and then proceed to the next phase.
- If a timeout and a response from the selected alert occur in the same cycle, the ping shall be treated as timed out and the failure indication shall be asserted.

## Escalation Ping Behavior

- The escalation channel to ping shall be selected deterministically in round-robin order, starting with channel zero after reset and wrapping from the last channel back to zero.
- Unlike alert channel selection, escalation selection shall not be randomized and shall not be affected by any enable mask.
- In the escalation ping phase, the module shall always assert an escalation ping request for the currently selected escalation channel.
- The module shall keep the escalation request asserted until the selected escalation channel responds or the ping timeout expires.
- If the selected escalation channel responds before timeout, the module shall proceed without reporting an escalation ping failure.
- If the timeout expires before the selected escalation channel responds, the module shall assert the escalation ping failure indication and then proceed to the next phase.
- The escalation channel index shall advance after the escalation ping phase completes, whether it completed by response or by timeout.
- Because the escalation order is deterministic and the wait/timeout phases are bounded, each escalation channel shall receive a ping at least once within a fixed maximum interval.

## Spurious Ping Response Detection

- The module shall monitor all incoming ping response indications against the currently active ping request.
- An incoming ping response shall be considered spurious if it is asserted for a channel that is not currently being requested.
- A response is also considered spurious if no ping request of that type is currently asserted.
- If a spurious alert response is detected, the module shall assert the alert ping failure indication.
- If a spurious escalation response is detected, the module shall assert the escalation ping failure indication.
- Spurious-response detection shall remain active in all phases, including while the module is inactive before enable and while waiting between pings.
- A response that remains asserted after the module has moved on from a ping request shall be treated as spurious on the cycle after the request is no longer active.

## Timeout and Failure Behavior

- The ping timeout value shall be programmed in clock cycles. The same value shall apply to alert and escalation ping attempts.
- A ping attempt shall be considered successful when the addressed channel responds before the timeout expires.
- A ping attempt shall be considered failed when the timeout expires before a response is received.
- On a timeout failure, the corresponding failure output shall be asserted.
- The module shall continue ping scheduling after a timeout failure; a single failed ping shall not permanently stop the scheduling unless an internal error is detected.
- The failure outputs are not sticky in themselves; they indicate the presence of the timeout or spurious-response condition on the cycle in which it occurs.

## Internal Error Handling

- The module shall protect its internal state with redundant, self-checking mechanisms.
- If an internal inconsistency is detected, such as a mismatch between redundant state copies or an invalid control-state value, the module shall enter a terminal error state.
- In the terminal error state:
  - the module shall stop issuing all new alert and escalation ping requests,
  - it shall assert both the alert ping failure and escalation ping failure indications continuously, and
  - it shall remain in that state until reset.

## Summary of Required Output Behavior

- Ping request outputs shall be deasserted except when a ping is actively waiting for a response.
- During an active alert ping, exactly one alert request shall be asserted.
- During an active escalation ping, exactly one escalation request shall be asserted.
- Alert ping failure shall be asserted for:
  - an alert ping timeout,
  - any spurious alert response, or
  - an internal error condition requiring terminal shutdown.
- Escalation ping failure shall be asserted for:
  - an escalation ping timeout,
  - any spurious escalation response, or
  - an internal error condition requiring terminal shutdown.
